instructions:
NEVER run git stash, git checkout, git reset, git restore, git clean, git merge, git rebase, git push, git commit, git mv or any command that changes the index, the stash stack, or other worktrees' state. Do NOT touch crates/ or any code. Do NOT write to /tmp. No `timeout` binary on this host: use the perl alarm form. DO NOT EXPLORE the code base: all facts are below. Read ONLY the four allowed docs, and only around the line ranges named. Edit the docs in your first substantive action, then run the verify commands. Do not commit.

FACTS ABOUT THE CLAUDE AGENT SDK TRANSPORT (all verified in code, tests and a live smoke against the real SDK; document exactly this, invent nothing):
- Claude no longer uses ACP and no longer needs the `claude-agent-acp` bridge package. Ajax runs a small Node sidecar (crates/ajax-web/sidecar/claude_sdk_sidecar.mjs, embedded in the ajax-web binary and started as `node --input-type=module -e <script>`, so no file is written to disk) that wraps the Claude Agent SDK `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` in ONE long-lived streaming-input `query()` per chat session. The sidecar speaks the same LF-delimited JSONL command/response framing the Pi RPC child uses, so the Rust side shares the same JSONL process wrapper, session driver and client core (`jsonl_process`, `rpc_session`, `rpc_client`). Claude-specific Rust: `claude_sdk_map` (SDK message -> adapter events), `claude_sdk_client`, `claude_sdk_spawn`. The transport is chosen by the core launch table: `AcpLaunch.transport` is `HarnessTransport::ClaudeSdk` for Claude, `PiRpc` for Pi, `Acp` for Cursor and Codex. Claude stays chat-capable (`acp_launch_for_agent(Claude)` is still `Some`, which is the 'supports Ajax Chat' predicate).
- Install: Node.js 20 or newer on PATH, plus `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`. The sidecar finds the SDK by package import, then `$(npm root -g)/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, then the copy nested in `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` (which is how it worked on a machine that still had the old bridge installed). A missing SDK makes the spawn fail with `no loadable claude-agent-sdk module; tried: ... - npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`. `ajax doctor` reports `sdk:claude` (checks `node`; the message names the install command). It no longer reports `acp:claude`. Codex keeps `acp:codex`; Pi keeps `rpc:pi`.
- Auth: the SDK uses the operator's existing Claude login; no API key is configured by Ajax. The SDK loads the operator's Claude settings (user, project, local), so hooks, plugins, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md apply to Ajax-started sessions just as they do in the Claude CLI.
- Protocol: first command `init` {cwd, model?, resume?}; the response carries the session id, the advertised models (`supportedModels()`), commands and the SDK initialization result; then `prompt`, `abort`, `set_model`, `set_effort`, `get_context_usage`, `shutdown`. Every SDK message the query yields is forwarded verbatim as an event.
- Session identity and restore: the Claude session id is the SDK session id, so sessions the old bridge created keep resuming. Restore relaunches with `resume: <id>` and is fail-closed twice: the sidecar looks the session up with the SDK's `getSessionInfo(id, { dir: cwd })` before resuming and answers `session not found: <id>` if it is missing (a lookup that throws or times out degrades to resuming; an SDK without `getSessionInfo` skips the check), and the client rejects a resume that answers with a different session id. Both surface as the typed `ACP restore unavailable` error (Retry / Start fresh); a session is never silently replaced.
- Model and effort: the model select is the SDK's advertised models (values such as `default`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, and variants like `claude-fable-5-1[1m]`); the effort select (category ThoughtLevel, id `effort`) offers low, medium, high, xhigh, max (a fixed list for now; the SDK reports per-model support). The option ids are `model` and `effort`, the same ids the ACP bridge advertised, so persisted pins such as `opus|effort=low` keep working. `set_model` rejects a value the SDK did not advertise (`unknown model: ...`); `set_effort` rejects levels outside the list. A pin that cannot be applied is reported as a model-apply error and never fails the spawn; later steps of the pin still apply.
- Streaming and usage: text and thinking arrive as stream deltas (the repeated text inside `assistant` messages is intentionally ignored so nothing shows twice); tool calls open from the stream and are completed from the `tool_result` message; the `result` message ends the turn and carries the usage, which becomes a context-usage update (used = input + cache creation + cache read + output tokens, window = the model's contextWindow) delivered BEFORE the finish; an aborted turn's all-zero usage is skipped so cancelling does not reset the context meter.
- Cancel: abort calls the SDK's `interrupt()`. The interrupted turn ends with an error_during_execution result (stopReason `cancelled`) and the SAME sidecar process accepts the next prompt; there is no respawn.
- Permissions and elicitation: the sidecar auto-allows every tool permission request (trusted-local, equivalent to the host auto-approve the ACP path used; there is no bypassPermissions flag) and always declines MCP elicitation requests (a known gap: the ACP path showed them as a form). The Claude variant of the session client rejects permission/elicitation responses.
- Security notes: an explicit `--sdk-module` override (used only by tests) is exclusive and never falls back to the installed SDK; the sidecar does not read an SDK module path from the environment; stdout lines from the child are capped at 16 MiB (`jsonl line exceeds ... bytes; discarded` error record) for both the Pi and Claude children.
- Known gaps (state them as such): image and audio prompt blocks are not forwarded (a placeholder line is sent); sub-agent (nested tool) traffic is dropped; effort levels are a fixed list.

ALSO TRUE NOW FOR PI (correct any sentence that says otherwise): Pi uses no ACP either; the ACP adapters that remain are Cursor (native `agent acp`) and Codex (`@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`). The doctor checks are `acp:codex`, `rpc:pi`, `sdk:claude`. Do not claim anything about Cursor or Codex that is not already in the docs.
